subject: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the demo and the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key points I captured:
- Your primary concern: noisy-neighbor effects on latency during peak batch inference jobs. You called out several customer workloads where tail latency spikes caused customer-facing timeouts.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints, with tight tail latency expectations for business-critical flows.
- Compliance/regulatory constraint: data residency and audit logging for a subset of traffic.
- Preferred deployment model: open to a Hosted API for fast iteration, but you want guaranteed isolation/SLOs for production-critical routes — potential need for Dedicated or Private (VPC) depending on isolation requirements.

Follow-ups from our side:
1) I'll pull together a short comparison doc (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) focused on isolation guarantees, latency SLOs we can commit to, and what telemetry we can provide.
2) We can share a sample SLO template and an example SLA for Dedicated capacity.
3) Proposed next step: 1-hour technical workshop with your infra + ML infra team to go over traffic patterns, peak QPS, batch jobs, and security requirements.

Are you available next week for a workshop? If you can share an ETA for expected peak QPS and a representative payload size (avg token length / request), we can draft a concrete capacity estimate and a short pilot plan.

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: (will follow)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the write-up, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Noisy neighbor: this is our biggest worry. We run both steady online traffic and large scheduled batch scoring jobs (nightly retrains + periodic reruns). In the past, batch runs on shared infra have caused tail latency to jump and led to failed customer requests.
- SLOs: we'd like to aim for p95 <= 150ms and keep p99 as low as possible (we don't have an exact number yet). If you can provide historical tail distributions for similar workloads or an isolation SLA for Dedicated, that would help.
- Private VPC: Preferable from a compliance standpoint, but if Dedicated can provide strict tenant isolation and audit logs (and a contractual SLA), that might be acceptable.

I'll attach the list of our compliance questions and a rough QPS range in a follow-up email. For the workshop, next Wednesday (24th) afternoon PT works for our infra lead.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Alex — great, thanks for the specifics. Quick answers and what we'll bring to the workshop: 

High-level deployment guidance (summary):
- Hosted API: Fastest time-to-value. We do not provide tenant-level isolation guarantees on Hosted; it's best for non-critical/early-stage traffic and iterative experimentation. Telemetry is available but not backed by dedicated isolation SLAs.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools for your account with configurable isolation boundaries. We can offer an SLA for availability and per-route latency targets (we typically commit to availability SLA + throughput guarantees; latency SLOs are common add-ons for Dedicated contracts). Dedicated isolates noisy-neighbor risk since you get reserved capacity and configurable scaling.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full network isolation and customer-managed control plane. Best for strict compliance/data residency requirements — also supports HSM/KMS integrations and audit logs under your tenancy.

What we'll bring to the workshop:
- A draft Dedicated SLA that covers availability, throughput, and a template for latency SLOs (we'll share the "slo-draft-20260618.docx").
- A short dedicated proposal with capacity/cost estimates based on the QPS and avg payload (draft attached: "redwood-dedicated-proposal-20260618.pdf").
- Examples of telemetry we can stream (per-request latency distributions, model-level token metrics, KV cache hit rates) and how we measure p95/p99.

Proposed pilot: 2–4 week Dedicated proof-of-concept with a small reserved pool to characterize tail behavior under your batch and online mix. We can instrument and provide daily regressions/alerts. If the compliance team still needs VPC, we can scope the Private deployment after the pilot.

Next actions: can you share (by EOD Monday) a rough QPS window, avg token lengths, and an example of a batch job size? That will let us size the pilot and bring an accurate cost estimate. Also, confirm that Wed 24th afternoon PT works and I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks,
Neha

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-20260618.pdf, slo-draft-20260618.docx
